criteria.text: The response identifies that Supply Agreement Section 14.2 treats a change in ownership of more than 50% of the Company's voting stock as an assignment requiring Vantrell's prior written consent, with a termination right if consent is not obtained. It also explains that the stock sale triggers this right while the SPA does not address it, because Section 4.4 / Disclosure Schedule 4.4 shows no required consents and the Section 7.2(c) closing condition does not cover it.

The response identifies that Supply Agreement Section 16.1 lets Vantrell (Supplier) assign the agreement without the Company's consent while the Company cannot assign without Supplier consent. It explains the risk that the sole-source supply contract could pass to a competitor or another undesirable party.

The response identifies that the Company's extension option under Supply Agreement Section 3.2 required notice at least 120 days before the December 31, 2026 end of the Initial Term, so the deadline fell on or about September 2, 2026. It states that this deadline had passed before the SPA was signed on September 21, 2026, and that the Extension Pricing / extension right is therefore lost or at risk.

The response identifies that Side Letter Section 2 redefines Fundamental Representations as only SPA Sections 4.1 and 4.2. It explains that, because SPA Section 11.11 gives the Side Letter precedence, the Capitalization (4.3) and Taxes (4.12) representations drop out of the uncapped carve-out and become subject to the 10% cap.

The response identifies that Side Letter Section 6 selects Delaware law and the Delaware Court of Chancery for indemnification disputes, which conflicts with the SPA's New York governing law (Section 11.8) and New York County forum (Section 11.9). It explains that the precedence clause lets the Side Letter control, which splits forums or law for indemnity claims.
The response states that the SPA's general indemnity cap is 10% of the Purchase Price, or equivalently $8,450,000 on the $84,500,000 price.
The response states that the SPA's order of precedence (Section 11.11) places the Side Letter above the SPA.
The response is organized as a memo addressed to the supervising partner. It gives each issue as a distinct item with the document and section, why it matters to Halvorsen, and a recommended fix.
The response orders issues by significance (most significant first) and includes a flag or list of points requiring a client call before responding to the other side.
The response does not state that the Company's Section 3.2 extension option remains exercisable or that the notice window is still open as of signing.
The response does not state that the Fundamental Representations remain uncapped for Capitalization and Taxes under the documents as currently drafted, or that the SPA controls over the Side Letter.
